Job Description First Stop Health runs a growing AWS platform. It is a set of containerized microservices on ECS, event streaming on Kafka, and a long-running Django/Celery application that we are steadily moving onto modern delivery practices. Everything we run in dev, staging and production is defined as code and shipped through automated pipelines. You will be the newest member of a small, hands-on cloud team. You will own well-scoped pieces of the platform from the start, and take on larger ones as you prove out. You will write Terraform, maintain GitHub Actions pipelines, keep services healthy and help make releases boring. This role suits an engineer who has already shipped infrastructure in a real environment and is ready to take more ownership of production, in a team that reviews changes carefully and values writing things down. Responsibilities Write and review Terraform for AWS resources (ECS Fargate, IAM, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, ALB, Cloud Map, MSK, RDS) using reusable modules and per-environment stacks. Build and maintain CI/CD in GitHub Actions: reusable workflows, OIDC-based AWS authentication (no long-lived keys), environment-scoped deploy roles, and build-once, promote-by-digest releases across dev, staging and production. Help move legacy delivery tooling (AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild) onto GitHub Actions, including task-definition templating and automated rollback on failed deploys. Carry production changes through our gate: produce a plan, get it reviewed, then apply. Keep dev, staging and production consistent, and detect and resolve drift. Operate containerized services: monitor service health, read logs to diagnose failures, investigate failed deployments and unhealthy targets, and document what you learn. Support observability: Datadog agents and log shipping, CloudWatch alarms and service health checks. Help close the gaps in service-health alerting. Contribute to our multi-account AWS foundation, managed with Atmos and Terraform components (networking, DNS, SSO and team roles, ECR, ECS, Aurora, ElastiCache, backups and logging), including pull requests, automated plans and applies, and drift detection. Help keep us audit-ready: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, backups, encryption and access reviews, working with our compliance tooling (Vanta). Work with the application teams on event-streaming infrastructure (Kafka on MSK, topics, IAM grants, consumer groups and Debezium change data capture). Apply least-privilege IAM and sound secrets handling. Never expose secret values or sensitive data in code, logs or pull requests. Take part in a rotating on-call (PagerDuty) schedule for production. You will respond to alerts, triage with the runbooks, escalate when needed, and write up what happened afterwards. New team members shadow the rotation before taking a primary shift. Keep runbooks and architecture notes current, and write clear pull requests that explain the what and the why. Requirements 2 to 4 years of experience in cloud, DevOps, platform or site reliability work, or equivalent hands-on experience. Working knowledge of AWS, including ECS or another container platform, IAM, S3, VPC networking and CloudWatch. Hands-on Terraform (or a comparable infrastructure-as-code tool): modules, remote state, and reading a plan critically before applying. Experience building CI/CD pipelines, preferably GitHub Actions. Comfort with Docker and containerized workloads. Solid Git skills (branching, rebasing, resolving conflicts, pull-request review) and the command line (bash). Scripting in Bash or Python, and fluency with JSON and YAML, including tools such as jq. Willingness to join a rotating on-call schedule, and a calm, methodical approach to incidents. Clear written communication, and the habit of checking your work against logs and real state rather than assumptions. Nice to Have Experience with Atmos, Terragrunt or another tool for managing Terraform across many accounts and stacks, and with Cloud Posse components or Geodesic. Experience with ecspresso, AWS CDK or CloudFormation, or other ECS deployment tooling. Familiarity with AWS Organizations and multi-account patterns: IAM Identity Center (SSO), SAML or Entra ID federation, Transit Gateway, VPC design and DNS delegation. Experience with AWS security and compliance services (CloudTrail, GuardDuty, AWS Backup, WAF) and with compliance platforms such as Vanta, in support of SOC 2 or HIPAA-style controls. Exposure to Aurora/RDS Postgres, ElastiCache (Redis), SQS, DMS or Lambda. Experience with self-hosted GitHub Actions runners, pre-commit hooks, terraform-docs and architecture decision records (ADRs). Exposure to Kafka or managed streaming (MSK), or change data capture with Debezium. Familiarity with Datadog or a similar observability platform. Experience running Django or Celery applications in production, or working with PostgreSQL / Aurora. Understanding of cross-account access patterns (for example, cross-account ECR pulls) and OIDC federation. Experience in a regulated environment such as healthcare, and an understanding of why data-handling discipline matters. An AWS certification (Solutions Architect Associate, DevOps Engineer Professional or similar). Tools you’ll work with Cloud: AWS (ECS Fargate, ECR, MSK, Aurora/RDS, ElastiCache, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, IAM Identity Center, CloudWatch) Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atmos, Geodesic, pre-commit, terraform-docs Delivery: GitHub Actions (including OIDC and reusable workflows), ecspresso, Docker Streaming and data: Kafka (MSK), Debezium, PostgreSQL Observability, security and compliance: Datadog, PagerDuty, CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Vanta Applications you will support: Medplum-based services, a Django/Celery monolith, and Kong How We Work Production changes are gated. Plan, human review, then apply. Nothing reaches production as a side effect of other work. Evidence over assumption. We diagnose from logs and real service state, and we report outcomes honestly, including failures. Security by default. Least-privilege IAM, encrypted storage, private-by-default buckets, and no secret values in output. Build once, promote everywhere. The artifact tested in dev is the artifact that reaches staging and production. Write it down. Runbooks, pull-request descriptions and lessons learned are part of the job. Review is normal. Infrastructure changes are reviewed by a peer before they ship. Shared on-call. The team rotates production on-call through PagerDuty, so no one carries it alone. Why join us Real ownership of production infrastructure, with a team that reviews and teaches. Meaningful work: reliable systems that support members' access to care. A modernization effort in progress, so you will see the full arc from legacy to automated delivery. First Stop Health is committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging.
